mainTopic: Splitting a לאו שבכללות through extra words in the פסוק, the power of a גזירה שוה, and the laws and recipe of שמן המשחה.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a discussion of לאו שבכללות, one prohibition that covers several items and normally earns only one set of מלקות. Extra words in a פסוק can split such a לאו, so eating each kind of מעשר שני outside ירושלים is punished separately. The same idea applies to לחם, קלי and כרמל eaten before the עומר. The גמרא proves that קלי is extra by learning it from לחם and כרמל together, and shows from its place in the middle of the פסוק that each food earns its own מלקות. Next, a series of sages (רבי ינאי, רבי סימאי, אביי and רב אשי) teach that a גזירה שוה must never be taken lightly. Major laws rest on one alone: כרת for פיגול and נותר, the ban and the burning penalty for בתו מאנוסתו, and סקילה for certain forbidden relations. The גמרא then turns to the משנה's case of blending שמן המשחה. It learns from the קטרת that blending it for the community is פטור, and explains why half a batch of oil is פטור while half a batch of קטרת is חייב. Finally it discusses the recipe of the oil: the weight of each spice, whether the spices are weighed with a small surplus, and how the oil was made. That last question is a debate between רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי, and רבי יהודה's reply continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The words 'You may not eat' make it a real prohibition
steps.stepSummary: The תורה wrote לא תוכל to turn eating מעשר שני outside ירושלים into a formal לאו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רחמנא wrote 'You may not eat' in order to establish it as a prohibition (לאו).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an answer from the earlier discussion. It explains that the phrase לא תוכל exists to make eating מעשר שני outside ירושלים a formal לאו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wording 'You may not' could have looked like a simple description of what you are unable to do. The גמרא reads it as a true prohibition. That means someone who breaks it can get מלקות.

keyTerms.meaning: A negative commandment, a prohibition that normally carries מלקות
'You may not' (the wording of the פסוק)
To establish it, to set it up as
The second tithe, which must be eaten in ירושלים

phrases.english: The Merciful One wrote: "You may not eat",
phrases.notes: דברים 12:17. The פסוק is about eating מעשר שני outside ירושלים.

phrases.english: to establish it as a prohibition.

steps.triggerLanguage: כתב רחמנא לא תוכל לאוקמה בלאו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes an answer from the discussion before this section.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words לא תוכל turn eating מעשר שני outside ירושלים into a formal לאו.

steps.title: But it is a general prohibition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that one לאו covering grain, wine and oil is a לאו שבכללות, which should not earn separate מלקות.
steps.simpleTranslation: But still, it is a general prohibition (לאו שבכללות)!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the previous step. Even if it is a real לאו, it covers three different items at once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A לאו שבכללות is one prohibition that lumps several things together. Normally you cannot get separate מלקות for each item in such a לאו. So how can each kind of מעשר count on its own?

keyTerms.meaning: A 'general prohibition': one לאו that covers several separate items
And still, even so

steps.confusionAlert: A לאו שבכללות is still a real prohibition. The question is only whether each item inside it earns its own separate set of מלקות.

phrases.english: But still, it is a general prohibition!

steps.triggerLanguage: ועדיין לאו שבכללות הוא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 1: a real לאו, but a lumped-together one.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that each type of מעשר שני carries its own punishment
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One לאו covering many items is a לאו שבכללות, and that normally does not earn separate מלקות.

steps.title: The extra listing of grain, wine and oil splits them up
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק could have just said 'them'. Listing each item shows that eating each one is its own prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let the פסוק say 'You may not eat them within your gates.' Why do I need 'the tithe of your grain, your wine and your oil'? To single out the eating of each one separately.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It points out that the פסוק spells out each item when it didn't need to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An earlier פסוק already mentioned the tithes, so 'them' would have been enough. Since the תורה listed grain, wine and oil one by one, each gets its own לאו. That means separate מלקות for each.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, if that were true
Why do I need it? (these words are extra)
To single out, to make each one separate
Grain, wine, oil

steps.whatToRemember: When the תורה lists items one by one when it didn't need to, each item becomes its own prohibition, even inside a לאו שבכללות.

phrases.english: If so, let the verse say:
"You may not eat them within your gates",
why do I need "the tithe of your grain, your wine, and your oil"?
To single out the eating of each and every one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אם כן נימא קרא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One לאו for all three items means only one set of מלקות.
steps.terutzMaskana: The extra listing makes each item a separate prohibition.

steps.title: Bread, parched grain and fresh stalks: three sets of lashes
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק rules that eating לחם, קלי and כרמל from new grain before the עומר earns three sets of מלקות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: One who eats bread, parched grain and fresh stalks gets three sets of מלקות.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins. רבי יצחק rules on eating new grain before the עומר offering is brought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק forbids all three foods in one sentence. Even so, רבי יצחק counts them as three separate punishments. This sets up the same problem as before.

keyTerms.meaning: Bread
Parched (roasted) grain
Fresh, soft stalks of grain
Gets מלקות (lashes)
The barley offering that permits eating the new grain

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said:
One who eats bread, parched grain, and fresh stalks –
phrases.notes: ויקרא 23:14. He means eating them from the new crop before the עומר is brought.

phrases.english: is flogged three times.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רבי יצחק האוכל לחם קלי וכרמל לוקה שלש
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new case on the same topic of separate מלקות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eating לחם, קלי and כרמל before the עומר earns three sets of מלקות.

steps.title: But there are no lashes for a general prohibition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that one לאו listing three foods is a לאו שבכללות.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we do not give מלקות for a general prohibition (לאו שבכללות)!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יצחק with the same rule it used before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All three foods appear in a single prohibition. By the normal rule, they should not earn three separate sets of מלקות.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not give מלקות
But surely

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אֵין לוֹקִין עַל לָאו שֶׁבִּכְלָלוֹת!
phrases.english: But one is not flogged for a general prohibition!

steps.triggerLanguage: והא אין לוקין על לאו שבכללות
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יצחק's ruling of three sets of מלקות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: No separate מלקות for items inside a לאו שבכללות.

steps.title: Here the verses are extra
steps.stepSummary: This case is different because the פסוק has extra words that split the three foods apart.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different here, because the verses are extra.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the פסוק did not need to name all three foods. That is what makes them separate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same idea as with מעשר שני: extra listing creates separate prohibitions. The גמרא now has to show exactly which words are extra.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different here
Extra, not needed for its plain meaning

phrases.english: It is different here, since the verses are superfluous –

steps.triggerLanguage: שאני הכא דמייתר קראי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Three foods in one לאו means one set of מלקות.
steps.terutzMaskana: The extra words make each food its own prohibition.

steps.title: Couldn't the verse just say 'bread'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tests the claim of extra words: maybe the פסוק only needed לחם, and the other two could be learned from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the פסוק say 'bread', and we would learn parched grain and fresh stalks from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins checking which words are truly extra. It suggests that only לחם was needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If קלי and כרמל could be learned from לחם, then those two words would be extra. That would support the answer in step 6. This is a setup line, and the next step tests it.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us learn it, derive it
From it

phrases.english: Let the verse say "bread",
and we will derive parched grain and fresh stalks from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: לימא קרא לחם ונילף קלי וכרמל מיניה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to show which words are extra, as step 6 claimed.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which of the three words are really extra?

steps.title: Bread is special because of challah
steps.stepSummary: You cannot learn קלי and כרמל from לחם, because לחם has an extra obligation of חלה that they lack.
steps.simpleTranslation: This can be refuted: what about bread? It is special, since it has an added obligation of חלה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggestion from step 7. It shows that לחם is too special to teach about the other two foods.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To learn one case from another, the cases must be alike. לחם is made from dough, so it has a חלה obligation, while קלי and כרמל do not. Because of this difference, the תורה may have needed to write them separately, so they are not obviously extra.

keyTerms.meaning: This can be refuted, the comparison has a flaw
What about...? It is special because... (a way to break a comparison)
The portion taken from dough for the כהן
Was given more, has an extra obligation

phrases.english: There is room to refute:
What about bread?
It is special, since it has an added obligation regarding challah!

steps.triggerLanguage: איכא למיפרך מה ללחם שכן נתרבה אצל חלה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the derivation proposed in step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that קלי and כרמל could be learned from לחם
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: לחם has a חלה obligation that קלי and כרמל lack, so it cannot serve as their source.

steps.title: Maybe only parched grain needed to be written
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the פסוק could have written only קלי and taught the other foods from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the verse write only 'parched grain' and not 'bread,' and we would learn the rest from parched grain.
steps.whatsHappening: Having rejected לחם as the source food in step 8, the גמרא now tries קלי as the one food from which the others could be learned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If לחם and כרמל could be learned from קלי, then writing them would be extra. The גמרא is testing whether the extra-words claim of step 6 holds up from this side.

keyTerms.meaning: Parched (roasted) kernels of grain
And let us learn (derive) it

phrases.english: Let it write 'parched grain' and not write 'bread,'
phrases.notes: He means the פסוק could have left out כרמל too, so only קלי would be written.

phrases.english: and we will learn from parched grain.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִכְתּוֹב קָלִי וְלָא לִכְתּוֹב לֶחֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After לחם failed as the source food, the גמרא tries קלי instead.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Could לחם and כרמל be learned from קלי, which would make their mention extra?

steps.title: Parched grain has special features the others lack
steps.stepSummary: Neither לחם nor כרמל can be learned from קלי, because קלי has a different feature from each of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Bread can't be learned from parched grain, because parched grain is still in its natural form and bread is not. Fresh stalks can't be learned from parched grain, because parched grain is used in meal offerings and fresh stalks are not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggestion from step 9 by showing how קלי is different from each of the other two foods.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Against לחם: קלי still looks like grain, while bread has been fully changed, so maybe only unchanged grain is forbidden. Against כרמל: קלי has a special role in מנחות and כרמל does not, so maybe only קלי is forbidden. Either way, the other foods must be written in the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: It is still in its original, recognizable form
Fresh, soft kernels still in the stalk
Has an extra role in meal offerings
Meal offerings brought from grain

phrases.english: Bread cannot come from parched grain,
because parched grain is in its original form,
while bread is not in its original form.
Fresh stalks cannot come from parched grain,
because parched grain has an extra role in meal offerings,
while fresh stalks have no extra role in meal offerings!

steps.triggerLanguage: לֶחֶם מִקָּלִי לָא אָתֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion of step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects learning both לחם and כרמל from קלי.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: קלי is unchanged (unlike לחם) and has a role in מנחות (unlike כרמל), so it cannot serve as the source for either.

steps.title: Maybe only fresh stalks needed to be written
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now tries כרמל as the single source food.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the verse write only 'fresh stalks,' and we would learn bread and parched grain from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the last remaining option: learning the other two foods from כרמל alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: לחם and קלי have both failed as the single source. If כרמל works, then לחם and קלי would be extra words.

keyTerms.meaning: From it

phrases.english: Let it write 'fresh stalks'
and we will learn bread and parched grain from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִכְתּוֹב כַּרְמֶל וְנֵילַף לֶחֶם וְקָלִי מִינֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After קלי failed, the גמרא tries כרמל.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Could לחם and קלי be learned from כרמל?

steps.title: Fresh stalks are completely unchanged
steps.stepSummary: כרמל cannot be the source, because it has not changed at all from its natural state.
steps.simpleTranslation: This can be refuted: fresh stalks are special because they have not changed from their original state at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects learning from כרמל by pointing to something special about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Perhaps only grain that is totally untouched is forbidden before the עומר. Then we could not apply the ban to roasted or baked grain, so those foods must be written.

keyTerms.meaning: There is room to refute it (point out a difference)
Has not changed from its original, natural state

phrases.english: It can be refuted:

phrases.aramaic: מָה לְכַרְמֶל שֶׁכֵּן לֹא נִשְׁתַּנָּה מִבְּרִיָּיתוֹ!
phrases.english: what about fresh stalks? They have not changed from their original state!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא לְמִיפְרַךְ: מָה לְכַרְמֶל שֶׁכֵּן לֹא נִשְׁתַּנָּה מִבְּרִיָּיתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion of step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects learning לחם and קלי from כרמל.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: כרמל is totally unchanged, unlike the other two.

steps.title: New approach: learn one food from the other two
steps.stepSummary: Since no single food can teach the other two, the גמרא proposes learning one food from two together.
steps.simpleTranslation: We cannot learn from one food alone. But let us learn one food from the other two!
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא changes strategy and gets ready to test each food as the one learned from the other two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every single food has failed as a source. Two foods together can be stronger, because a special feature of one may be missing in the other, so that feature cannot be the reason for the law.

keyTerms.meaning: We cannot learn from one alone
One from two

phrases.english: From one, they cannot be learned,
let us learn one from two?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִן חַד לָא יָלְפִי, נֵילַף חֲדָא מִן תְּרֵין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sums up the failures of steps 8 through 12 and opens a new kind of derivation.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Can one of the three foods be learned from the other two, making its mention extra?

steps.title: Try learning bread from the other two
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proposes leaving out לחם and learning it from קלי and כרמל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the verse not write 'bread,' and we would learn it from parched grain and fresh stalks.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the first option: לחם as the food learned from the other two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If לחם could be learned from קלי and כרמל, then the word לחם would be extra.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק (verse)

phrases.english: Let the verse not write 'bread'
and we will learn it from parched grain and fresh stalks –

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא נִכְתּוֹב קְרָא לֶחֶם וְנֵילַף מִקָּלִי וְכַרְמֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the plan of step 13 to לחם.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Could לחם be learned from קלי and כרמל together?

steps.title: Both sources are still in natural form
steps.stepSummary: קלי and כרמל share a feature that לחם lacks: they are still recognizable grain.
steps.simpleTranslation: This can be refuted: parched grain and fresh stalks are both still in their original form.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects learning לחם from the other two by finding a feature both of them share.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two sources only help if no shared feature sets them apart. Here קלי and כרמל are both still grain kernels, while לחם is fully changed, so לחם must be written on its own.

keyTerms.meaning: That they are still in their original form

phrases.english: It can be refuted:
what about parched grain and fresh stalks? They are in their original form!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא לְמִיפְרַךְ: מָה לְקָלִי וְכַרְמֶל דְּאִיתַנְהוֹן בְּעֵינֵיהוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proposal of step 14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects learning לחם from קלי and כרמל.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Both sources share being unprocessed, which לחם is not.

steps.title: Try learning fresh stalks from the other two
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proposes leaving out כרמל and learning it from לחם and קלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the verse not write 'fresh stalks,' and we would learn it from bread and parched grain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the second option: כרמל as the food learned from the other two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If this works, the word כרמל would be extra in the פסוק.

phrases.english: Let the verse not write 'fresh stalks'
and we will learn it from bread and parched grain –

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא נִכְתּוֹב קְרָא כַּרְמֶל וְנֵילַף מִלֶּחֶם וְקָלִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After לחם failed, applies the plan of step 13 to כרמל.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Could כרמל be learned from לחם and קלי together?

steps.title: Both sources are used in meal offerings
steps.stepSummary: לחם and קלי share a role in מנחות that כרמל lacks.
steps.simpleTranslation: This can be refuted: bread and parched grain both have an extra role in meal offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects learning כרמל from the other two, because they share a feature that כרמל does not have.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both לחם and קלי play a part in מנחות, but כרמל does not. Perhaps that shared role is why they are forbidden, so כרמל must be written on its own.

keyTerms.meaning: They have an extra role or added obligation

phrases.english: It can be refuted:

phrases.aramaic: מָה לְלֶחֶם וְקָלִי שֶׁכֵּן נִתְרַבּוּ אֵצֶל מְנָחוֹת!
phrases.english: what about bread and parched grain? They have an extra role in meal offerings!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא לְמִיפְרַךְ: מָה לְלֶחֶם וְקָלִי שֶׁכֵּן נִתְרַבּוּ אֵצֶל מְנָחוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proposal of step 16.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects learning כרמל from לחם and קלי.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Both sources share a role in מנחות that כרמל lacks.

steps.title: Parched grain can be learned from bread and fresh stalks
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק shows that קלי can be learned from לחם and כרמל, because each one's special feature is missing in the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק could tell you: Let the verse not write 'parched grain,' and we would learn it from bread and fresh stalks. What would you object? If you say bread is special because it has the obligation of חלה, fresh stalks prove that doesn't matter. If you say fresh stalks are special because they are unchanged, bread proves that doesn't matter!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי יצחק by finding the one pair that works: learning קלי from לחם and כרמל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each source has its own special feature, but the other source lacks that feature and is still forbidden. לחם has חלה but כרמל does not; כרמל is unchanged but לחם is changed. Since no special feature explains both, the ban must come from what they share, and that applies to קלי too.

keyTerms.meaning: What objection would you raise?
The portion of dough given to a כהן
Will prove (that this feature is not the reason)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't ask why קלי's own role in מנחות doesn't block this. Here קלי is the food being learned, not a source. We only need to show that the sources' special features don't matter.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzḥak could say to you:
Let the verse not write 'parched grain,'
and we will learn it from bread and fresh stalks.
What would you refute?
If you refute: what about bread?
It has an extra obligation of חלה –
fresh stalks will prove otherwise!
phrases.notes: כרמל has no חלה, yet it is still forbidden, so חלה can't be the reason.

phrases.english: And if it is because fresh stalks
have not changed from their original state –
bread will prove otherwise!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ רַבִּי יִצְחָק: לָא נִכְתּוֹב קְרָא קָלִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After two pairs failed, finds the third pair that works, which defends רבי יצחק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Derivation from two sources that answer each other's objections
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every way of learning one food from the others fails, so no word in the פסוק is extra.
steps.terutzMaskana: קלי can be learned from לחם and כרמל, so its mention is extra.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the basic method of learning from two sources: each source's special feature is cancelled out by the other source.

steps.title: So one gets lashes for each food
steps.stepSummary: Since קלי is extra in the פסוק, the foods are split into separate לאוין, and one receives מלקות for each.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore he is flogged for each one, because the verse is extra.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that רבי יצחק's ruling stands: three sets of מלקות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Writing קלי was not needed to teach that it is forbidden. So the extra word teaches that the foods are separate, and this answers the לאו שבכללות question from step 5.

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore
He receives מלקות (lashes)
Because it is extra (not needed for its plain teaching)

steps.whatToRemember: One food can't teach the others, and לחם or כרמל can't be learned from two. But קלי can be learned from לחם and כרמל. So קלי is extra, and that extra word splits the three foods into three separate לאוין.

phrases.english: Therefore he is flogged, because it is extra.
phrases.notes: He means he is flogged for each food separately, just as רבי יצחק ruled.

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Eating לחם, קלי and כרמל of new grain before the עומר earns three sets of מלקות, because the extra mention of קלי splits the לאו.

steps.title: Maybe only parched grain gets its own lashes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the conclusion. Perhaps the extra word קלי only gives קלי its own set of מלקות, while לחם and כרמל together get one shared set.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe say this: for קלי, which is extra in the פסוק, a person gets one set of lashes, and for all the others together he gets just one set.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on step 19. It suggests a smaller reading of the extra קלי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 19 said the extra קלי splits all three foods into separate לאוין. The challenge says the extra word might only separate קלי itself. Then לחם and כרמל would stay together under one general prohibition, with only one set of מלקות.

keyTerms.meaning: Which is extra (not needed for its own teaching)
He is liable to one (set of lashes)
For all of them (the rest)

phrases.english: But say: for parched grain, which is extra, one is liable to one set of lashes,
and for all the rest of them one is liable to just one!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵימָא

steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion that all three foods are separate לאוין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An extra word may only make its own item stand alone. It need not split up the other items.

steps.title: Parched grain is in the middle to link both sides
steps.stepSummary: If only קלי were meant to stand alone, the פסוק would have put it first or last. Putting it in the middle shows that לחם and כרמל each take on קלי's separate status.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the פסוק should have written "bread, fresh stalks, and parched grain," or "parched grain, bread, and fresh stalks." Why did it put קלי in the middle? This is what it means: bread is punished like קלי, and fresh stalks are punished like קלי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from the order of the words in the פסוק. Since קלי is in the middle, it applies its separate punishment to both sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Placing an item at the start or end would have set it apart from the others as a unique item. Placing it between לחם and כרמל connects it to each of them. So each food gets its own separate לאו and its own set of מלקות, which confirms step 19.

Alternatively

steps.title: Never take a verbal analogy lightly: the case of פיגול
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי opens a new topic. A גזירה שוה is very powerful, since the כרת for פיגול, a major Torah law, is known only through one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ינאי said: Never treat a גזירה שוה as minor in your eyes. פיגול is one of the main laws of the Torah, yet the Torah taught it only through a גזירה שוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new statement about how important a גזירה שוה is. It uses פיגול as the example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think a law learned from a matching word is weaker than one written clearly. רבי ינאי shows that the punishment of כרת for eating פיגול comes only from a גזירה שוה. The next step will show which one.

keyTerms.meaning: A verbal analogy: learning a law from the same word used in two places
An offering brought with the intent to eat it after its allowed time
The main, central laws of the Torah
Light (unimportant) in your eyes

phrases.english: A verbal analogy should never be light in your eyes,

phrases.english: and the verse taught it only through a verbal analogy.

steps.title: The source: פיגול learns כרת from נותר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the actual גזירה שוה. Both נותר and פיגול use the words "shall bear his iniquity," so פיגול gets כרת just like נותר.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי יוחנן said in the name of what זבדא בר לוי taught: It says there, about נותר, "Whoever eats it shall bear his iniquity." It says here, about פיגול, "The soul that eats from it shall bear its iniquity." Just as there the punishment is כרת, so too here it is כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רבי ינאי by showing the exact גזירה שוה. It is the one that gives פיגול the punishment of כרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about פיגול says "shall bear iniquity" but never says כרת. The same phrase appears by נותר, where כרת is mentioned. Because the same words are used, the כרת of נותר carries over to פיגול.

keyTerms.meaning: There (in the other place in the Torah)
Here (in the place we are learning about)

steps.title: Never take a verbal analogy lightly: the case of נותר
steps.stepSummary: רבי סימאי says the same thing about נותר. Its punishment, which is also the base for the law of פיגול, is also learned only through a גזירה שוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי סימאי said: Never treat a גזירה שוה as minor in your eyes. נותר is one of the main laws of the Torah, yet the Torah taught it only through a גזירה שוה.
steps.whatsHappening: A second sage repeats the same idea, this time about נותר. This sets up the גמרא to show where נותר's own punishment comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 23 learned פיגול from נותר. Now רבי סימאי says that even נותר's punishment of כרת is itself learned from a גזירה שוה. So the chain of laws rests on these analogies.

steps.title: The word 'sacred' links נותר to its punishment
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא names the גזירה שוה for נותר. The word קדש appears in a verse with a punishment and also in a verse openly about נותר.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is this גזירה שוה? We learn it from the word 'sacred' in two places. One verse says: 'Those who eat it shall bear his iniquity, for he has profaned the sacred thing of ה'.' Another verse says: 'You shall burn the leftover in fire, for it is sacred.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which גזירה שוה רבי סימאי was talking about. It answers by showing that the word קדש appears in two verses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse in ויקרא gives a punishment, 'shall bear his iniquity,' but does not openly say it is about נותר. The verse in שמות openly talks about נותר. Since both use the word קדש, the punishment in ויקרא is applied to נותר.

keyTerms.meaning: Sacred; the shared word that links the two verses
He shall bear his iniquity; wording that points to a severe punishment
Meat of a קרבן left over past the time it may be eaten

steps.title: Never treat a גזירה שוה lightly
steps.stepSummary: אביי teaches that a גזירה שוה is powerful. The ban on a man's daughter from a woman he raped is a core Torah law, yet it is known only through a גזירה שוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Never think a גזירה שוה is minor. The law about a man's daughter from a woman he raped is one of the core laws of the Torah, and the Torah teaches it only through a גזירה שוה.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי adds a new example to the theme of רבי ינאי and רבי סימאי. He points to the case of בתו מאנוסתו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier examples were about קדשים, meaning פיגול and נותר. אביי brings a case from forbidden relationships. This shows that the power of a גזירה שוה is not limited to one area of the Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: A man's daughter born from a woman he raped
The core, major laws of the Torah
Light or minor in your eyes

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גזירה שוה is powerful. The law of בתו מאנוסתו is learned only through one.

steps.title: The word הנה teaches the ban
steps.stepSummary: Through רבא, רבי יצחק בר אבדימי teaches that the ban on בתו מאנוסתו comes from the word הנה, which appears in two verses.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבא said: רבי יצחק בר אבדימי told me that the word הנה in one verse and הנה in another verse teach the ban.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up אביי's claim. It shows the actual גזירה שוה that makes this relationship forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One verse uses הנה about a man's granddaughters, which applies to granddaughters from a woman he raped. The other verse uses הנה about a woman and her daughter. The shared word links the two verses, so the man's own daughter from that woman is forbidden as well.

keyTerms.meaning: They; an unusual word form, which is why it can be used for a גזירה שוה
For the prohibition itself

steps.title: The word זמה teaches the punishment of burning
steps.stepSummary: A second גזירה שוה uses the word זמה. It teaches that the punishment for this sin is שריפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The word 'lewdness' in one verse and 'lewdness' in another teach the punishment of burning.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא gives the punishment. Like the ban itself, the punishment also comes only from a גזירה שוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 27 only showed that the act is forbidden. Here the word זמה links to the verse that gives שריפה for a man with a woman and her mother. So both the ban and the punishment rest on גזירות שוות, which proves אביי's point.

keyTerms.meaning: Lewdness; the shared word in the second גזירה שוה

steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives one more example, like אביי's and רבי סימאי's, of a major Torah law that comes only from a גזירה שוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is the same as in the earlier steps: a גזירה שוה can create a law with a death penalty. This time the example is סקילה (stoning) for certain forbidden relations, which the Torah never states openly for those cases.

steps.title: The words 'their blood is upon them' teach stoning
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows the גזירה שוה: the words דמיהם בם appear both by forbidden relations and by אוב and ידעוני, and the second verse clearly says stoning.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: It says here, 'their blood is upon them,' and it says about אוב and ידעוני, 'their blood is upon them.' Just as there the punishment is stoning, so too here it is stoning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show exactly which גזירה שוה רב אשי was talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the verses about forbidden relations, the Torah says 'their blood is upon them' but does not say how they die. By אוב and ידעוני the same words appear together with an open mention of stoning. The matching words carry the stoning over to the forbidden relations.

steps.title: Blending the anointing oil: when one is exempt and when liable
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the משנה's case of blending שמן המשחה. A ברייתא says blending it to learn or to give to the community is פטור, but blending it to smear on oneself is חייב.

steps.whatToRemember: The conclusion is that the spices are weighed with a slight surplus. The proof is that cinnamon is split into two weighings.

steps.title: Then what does 'בד בבד' mean?
steps.stepSummary: If there is a surplus, what does 'בד בבד' come to teach?
steps.simpleTranslation: And what does 'part for part' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that a surplus has been accepted, the גמרא asks how to read the פסוק that אביי used. This sets up רבינא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי read 'בד בבד' as requiring an exact weight. That reading has been rejected, so the phrase needs a new meaning.

keyTerms.meaning: And what (does it mean)?

phrases.english: And what is "part for part"?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי ״בַּד בְּבַד״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from the conclusion of step 45, which removed אביי's reading of the פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of 'בד בבד' now that the weighing includes a surplus.

steps.title: רבינא: don't weigh one spice against another
steps.stepSummary: רבינא explains that 'בד בבד' forbids putting one weighed spice on the scale as the weight for the next spice.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: it means one should not put one weight against another weight and weigh that way.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא gives a new meaning to 'בד בבד'. Each spice must be weighed on its own against the real weights, not against another spice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since each weighing has a surplus, weighing a spice against an already weighed spice would pile up the extras unevenly. 'בד בבד' teaches that each spice is measured separately against the standard weight.

keyTerms.meaning: One weight against another weight
Should place

phrases.english: Ravina said:
That he should not place a weight against a weight
phrases.notes: He means: don't use a spice you already weighed as the counterweight for the next spice.

phrases.english: and weigh.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבִינָא: שֶׁלֹּא יַנִּיחַ מִשְׁקָל בְּמִשְׁקָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 46.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'בד בבד' means each spice is weighed independently against standard weights, not against another spice.
steps.whatToRemember: Each spice is weighed with a slight surplus, and each one is weighed by itself. 'בד בבד' forbids weighing one spice against another.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: The roots were cooked directly in the anointing oil
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי יהודה, who says that משה made the שמן המשחה by cooking the spice roots in the oil itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: the anointing oil that משה made in the wilderness was made by cooking the roots in it. This is the opinion of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about how the שמן המשחה was physically made. רבי יהודה gives the first opinion: the spice roots were cooked right inside the oil.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the discussion was about weighing the spices. Now the question is how the spices got their scent into the oil. רבי יהודה's answer is the simplest one: put the roots in the oil and cook them together.

keyTerms.meaning: The holy anointing oil made by משה in the wilderness
The roots, meaning the spice roots and woods used for the oil
He cooks or boils it

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
The anointing oil that Moshe made in the wilderness –
he would cook the roots in it,
phrases.notes: The "roots" are the spices for the oil. רבי יהודה means they were boiled right inside the oil itself.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שֶׁמֶן הַמִּשְׁחָה שֶׁעָשָׂה מֹשֶׁה בְמִדְבַּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from how the spices were weighed to how the oil was actually prepared
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, the spice roots were cooked directly in the anointing oil.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: There was not enough oil even to coat the roots
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי challenges רבי יהודה. The amount of oil was too small even to smear on the roots, so the roots could not have been cooked in it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said to him: But the oil is not even enough to smear on the roots!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי attacks רבי יהודה's method. He says the oil was so little that the roots would soak it all up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The attack is practical. If the oil cannot even coat the roots, then cooking the roots in it is impossible. The oil would be absorbed and nothing would be left.

keyTerms.meaning: But surely, an opening that brings a strong objection
To smear or coat
Enough, sufficient

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said to him:
But it is not even enough to smear on the roots!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: וַהֲלֹא לָסוּךְ הָעִיקָּרִין אֵינוֹ סִיפֵּק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly challenges רבי יהודה's method
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's claim that the roots were cooked inside the oil
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The amount of oil is too small even to coat the roots, so cooking them in it would use up all the oil.

steps.title: רבי יוסי's method: Boil roots in water, float the oil on top, then skim it off
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי explains how the oil was really made. The roots were boiled in water and the oil was floated on top to absorb the scent. Then the oil was skimmed off.
steps.simpleTranslation: How did he do it? They brought the roots and boiled them in water. He floated the anointing oil on top of them, it absorbed the scent, and he skimmed it off.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי gives his own way of making the oil. This way avoids his own objection.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The roots are cooked in water, not in oil, so no oil gets soaked up by the roots. The oil only sits on top of the water, picks up the scent, and is then taken off whole. This way the small amount of oil is not lost.

keyTerms.meaning: How does he do it? It introduces the correct method
He floated, poured so it sits on top
Absorbed, took in
He skimmed it off or removed it

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה: the roots were cooked in the oil. רבי יוסי: the roots were boiled in water, the oil floated on top to absorb the scent, and then it was skimmed off.

phrases.english: How does he do it?
They brought the roots and boiled them in water,
and he floated the anointing oil over them,
and it absorbed the scent,
and he skimmed it off.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיצַד עוֹשֶׂה? הֵבִיאוּ הָעִיקָּרִין וּשְׁלָקוּם בְּמַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting רבי יהודה's method, רבי יוסי offers his own method
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוסי, the roots were boiled in water, the oil floated on top and absorbed the scent, and then it was removed.
